segmentation.text: The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour
if during the last one hundred feet of his approach to such intersection
does not have a clear and unobstructed view of such intersection
and of any traffic upon all of the streets or highways entering such intersection
for a distance of one hundred feet along all such streets or highways
except on a through street or highway

elements.justification: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s is the speed the limit bounds; its exclusion of acceleration does not apply.

st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'); traversing it is the subject's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). Its exclusion 'a crosswalk or a stop line' does not apply: the region itself is read.

'the last one hundred feet of his approach' is a .path window, reading kin.path_length 'distance travelled along the body's path', ending at the observation at which the subject's occupancy of j (rel.occupies, st.intersection) rose; the window is the subject's own path before that entry.

'the driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is read through the controlled motion of the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate's exclusion of 'who drives or controls a vehicle' is respected: the role is read through motion, the aggregate gives the class.

st.sight_distance 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... whether or not any road user is there': the view of the intersection is clear where the sight distance at the subject's point is at least the ground distance from its body to j (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'). Its exclusions (rel.visible, env.visibility) do not apply: the view of a place, not of an actual road user, is read.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. The streets or highways entering j are the ways w (st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') with st.on_way(j, w) ('an intersection lies on every way that meets there'). A view of any traffic upon them is, for every traffic member o occupying w (rel.occupies) whose ground distance to j (st.region_geometry) is within one hundred feet, rel.visible(subject, o) 'an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body'; its exclusion of the sight distance of a place does not apply since d8 carries that.

st.sight_along_way 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye ...; the smaller of the two directions' is read for every way w with st.on_way(j, w) and compared with the literal one hundred feet; its exclusions (st.sight_distance, rel.visible) do not apply: the sight along each entering way is what the words measure.

DEF-NRS-484A-275 'at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device': the subject's approach carrier c (the carrier it occupied, st.lane_enters(c, j), at the last observation before its entry into j) is governed (dev.governs) by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red traffic signal, while another carrier entering j is governed by one of them. Same reading as LVMC_11_12_070_B s7. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply.

A traffic-controlled intersection is one whose traffic a control device controls: a traffic signal ('a signal head') in a state other than dark, a stop sign or a yield sign governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') j itself or a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, j). dev.governs 'no closure to the lanes that enter it' is respected by reading both the junction and the entering carriers explicitly.

residues.why: every intersection is, by DEF-NRS-484A-105, a junction of highways and streets; the words add no region beyond the intersection whose approach the condition measures, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies an intersection j (st.intersection); and at some observation of the .path window of one hundred feet (kin.path_length) behind the observation at which its occupancy of j rose, the view was not clear: the subject's st.sight_distance was below its ground distance to j, or for some way w with st.on_way(j, w) its st.sight_along_way(w) was below one hundred feet, or some traffic member o (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying such a w within one hundred feet of j (st.region_geometry distance) was not rel.visible from the subject; and not (d9) the subject's approach carrier at its entry into j was governed by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal while another carrier entering j was governed by one; and not (d10) a traffic signal in a state other than dark, a stop sign or a yield sign governs j or a carrier entering j.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject occupies j, its kin.speed is at most fifteen miles per hour.

narrowings.why: a prima facie limit is read as a maximum: a speed above it is reported violated; the rebuttal a court may admit is not modelled
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
the legal designation 'through street or highway' is read through the devices on the road that display it (stop sign, yield sign, flashing-red signal governing the entering approaches)

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection, hedges limit sight along the cross street to 20 m during the last 100 ft of the subject's approach; it traverses j above fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, traversing j at or below fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same restricted view, but a traffic signal (circular_green) governs the subject's approach lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection; the source does not supply sight along the ways, and the subject traverses above fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection, no other road user in the scene; a wall limits sight along one cross way below one hundred feet during the last 100 ft of the approach; the subject traverses at or below fifteen mph. The traffic quantifier is empty and the verdict is still decided by the sight along the way.
